notes:
A. Dadabhai Naoroji

1. Dadabhai Naoroji — Overview

  • Dadabhai Naoroji was one of the earliest major economic critics of British rule in India.
  • He was a founder-member of the Indian National Congress.
  • His analysis of colonial economic exploitation became known as the Drain Theory.
📌 Must-Memorise

Dadabhai Naoroji → Drain Theory + Grand Old Man of India

2. Birth

  • Dadabhai Naoroji was born on 4 September 1825 in Bombay.
📌 Must-Memorise

Naoroji → 4 September 1825

3. Popular Title

  • He is popularly called the Grand Old Man of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Grand Old Man of India → Dadabhai Naoroji

4. Elphinstone Institution

  • Naoroji studied at Elphinstone Institution in Bombay.
  • He later became a professor there.

5. Academic Distinction

  • Naoroji became one of the earliest Indians to hold a professorial position at Elphinstone.

6. London Indian Society

  • Naoroji established the London Indian Society in 1865.
📌 Must-Memorise

London Indian Society → Dadabhai Naoroji

7. East India Association

  • He founded the East India Association in London in 1866.
📌 Must-Memorise

East India Association → 1866 → Dadabhai Naoroji

8. Purpose

The East India Association sought to:

  • Present Indian grievances before British opinion.
  • Discuss Indian administration.
  • Build political awareness in Britain.

9. Indian National Congress

  • Naoroji became one of the most important leaders of the early Moderate phase of the Congress.

10. Congress Presidencies

He presided over the INC sessions at:

  • Calcutta → 1886.
  • Lahore → 1893.
  • Calcutta → 1906.
📌 Must-Memorise

Naoroji → INC President Three Times

11. Calcutta Session — 1906

  • At the 1906 Calcutta session, Swaraj became an explicit major Congress objective.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Calcutta 1906 → Dadabhai Naoroji → Swaraj

12. British Parliament

  • Naoroji was elected to the British House of Commons in 1892.
📌 Must-Memorise

Dadabhai Naoroji → British Parliament → 1892

13. Constituency

  • He represented Finsbury Central as a Liberal Party member.

14. Historical First

  • Naoroji became the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Indian MP in British House of Commons → Dadabhai Naoroji

15. Drain Theory

  • Naoroji argued that British colonial rule continuously transferred wealth from India to Britain.
📌 Must-Memorise

Drain Theory → Dadabhai Naoroji

16. Mechanisms of Drain

He identified factors such as:

  • Salaries and pensions of British officials.
  • Home Charges.
  • Profits remitted abroad.
  • Military and administrative expenditure outside India.

17. Poverty and Un-British Rule in India

  • Naoroji's famous economic work was Poverty and Un-British Rule in India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Poverty and Un-British Rule in India → Dadabhai Naoroji

18. Significance of Drain Theory

  • It gave Indian nationalism an economic critique of colonialism.
  • Later nationalists expanded this argument.

19. Moderate Methods

Naoroji initially relied on:

  • Petitions.
  • Constitutional agitation.
  • Parliamentary pressure.
  • Public opinion.

20. Historical Importance

  • He connected:
  • Economic nationalism.
  • Constitutional politics.
  • Early Congress development.
B. Gopal Krishna Gokhale

  • Gopal Krishna Gokhale was one of the leading Moderates of the Indian National Congress.
  • He was a teacher, economist, legislator and political mentor.
📌 Must-Memorise

Gokhale → Moderate + Servants of India Society + Gandhi's Political Mentor

22. Birth

  • Gokhale was born on 9 May 1866 in the Ratnagiri region of Maharashtra.

23. Mahadev Govind Ranade

  • Justice M.G. Ranade was one of Gokhale's most important intellectual and political mentors.
📌 Must-Memorise

Gokhale's Mentor → M.G. Ranade

24. Deccan Education Society

  • Gokhale was associated with the Deccan Education Society.
📌 Must-Memorise

Gokhale → Deccan Education Society

25. Fergusson College

  • He taught at Fergusson College in Pune.

26. Indian National Congress

  • Gokhale became a leading voice of the Moderate wing.

27. Benares Congress

  • Gokhale presided over the Benares session of the INC in 1905.
📌 Must-Memorise

Benares Congress 1905 → Gopal Krishna Gokhale

28. Imperial Legislative Council

  • Gokhale became a member of the Imperial Legislative Council.

29. Budget Speeches

  • His budget speeches were famous for detailed criticism of:
  • Taxation.
  • Military expenditure.
  • Poverty.
  • Education policy.

30. Servants of India Society

  • Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.
📌 Must-Memorise

Servants of India Society → 1905 → Gokhale

31. Purpose

The Society aimed to train people for:

  • Public service.
  • Education.
  • National work.
  • Social reform.

32. Gandhi's Political Mentor

  • Gandhi regarded Gokhale as his political mentor in India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Gandhi's Political Guru → Gopal Krishna Gokhale

33. Gokhale in South Africa

  • Gokhale visited South Africa in 1912.
  • He met Gandhi and studied the condition of Indians there.

34. Political Method

  • Gokhale favoured gradual constitutional reform rather than revolutionary violence.

35. Tilak–Gokhale Contrast

Gokhale:

  • Moderate.
  • Constitutional methods.

Tilak:

  • Assertive nationalism.
  • Mass mobilisation.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite

Moderate → Gokhale

Extremist/Assertive → Tilak

36. Death

  • Gokhale died on 19 February 1915.
C. Bal Gangadhar Tilak

37. Bal Gangadhar Tilak — Overview

  • Tilak was one of the principal leaders of assertive nationalism.
  • He helped transform nationalism from elite petitions toward wider public mobilisation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tilak → Lokmanya + Kesari + Home Rule + Swaraj

38. Birth

  • Tilak was born on 23 July 1856 in Maharashtra.

39. Popular Title

  • He was popularly known as Lokmanya Tilak.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lokmanya → Bal Gangadhar Tilak

40. New English School

  • Tilak and his associates helped establish the New English School at Pune in 1880.

41. Deccan Education Society

  • He helped establish the Deccan Education Society in 1884.

42. Newspapers

Tilak was closely associated with:

  • Kesari → Marathi.
  • The Mahratta → English.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kesari → Marathi → Tilak

Mahratta → English → Tilak

43. Newspapers — 1881

  • Kesari and The Mahratta began publication in 1881.

44. Ganapati Festival

  • Tilak popularised the public Ganapati festival as an instrument of political mobilisation from the 1890s.
📌 Must-Memorise

Public Ganapati Festival → Tilak

45. Shivaji Festival

  • Tilak also promoted public celebrations honouring Chhatrapati Shivaji.
📌 Must-Memorise

Shivaji Festival → Tilak

46. Purpose of Festivals

They enabled:

  • Political meetings.
  • Nationalist education.
  • Wider popular participation.

47. Swaraj

  • Tilak is famously associated with the declaration that Swaraj was his birthright.
📌 Must-Memorise

"Swaraj is my birthright" → Tilak

48. Lal-Bal-Pal

The trio consisted of:

  • Lala Lajpat Rai.
  • Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
  • Bipin Chandra Pal.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lal-Bal-Pal → Lajpat Rai + Tilak + Bipin Pal

49. Sedition Cases

  • Tilak was repeatedly prosecuted for sedition by the British government.

50. 1897 Imprisonment

  • He was imprisoned following a major sedition prosecution in 1897.

51. 1908 Sedition Case

  • Tilak was again convicted of sedition in 1908.

52. Mandalay

  • He was transported to Mandalay prison in Burma.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tilak → Mandalay Imprisonment

53. Imprisonment Period

  • Tilak remained imprisoned in Mandalay from 1908 to 1914.

54. Gita Rahasya

  • Tilak wrote his famous work Gita Rahasya during the Mandalay imprisonment.
📌 Must-Memorise

Gita Rahasya → Bal Gangadhar Tilak

55. Home Rule League

  • Tilak established his Home Rule League in 1916.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tilak Home Rule League → 1916

56. Annie Besant

  • Annie Besant organised another major Home Rule League during the same period.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Home Rule → Tilak + Annie Besant

57. Lucknow Congress

  • Tilak's return to mainstream Congress politics was associated with the reunion of Moderates and Extremists at Lucknow in 1916.

58. Lucknow Pact

  • Congress and Muslim League also reached the Lucknow Pact in 1916.

59. Death

  • Tilak died on 1 August 1920.
📌 Must-Memorise

Tilak → Died 1 August 1920

Lajpat Rai → Mandalay → 1907

Young India:

70. Unhappy India

  • Lajpat Rai wrote Unhappy India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Unhappy India → Lala Lajpat Rai

71. Calcutta Special Session — 1920

  • Lajpat Rai presided over the Special Calcutta Session of the INC in 1920.
📌 Must-Memorise

Special Calcutta Congress 1920 → Lala Lajpat Rai

72. Servants of the People Society

  • Lajpat Rai founded the Servants of the People Society in 1921.
📌 Must-Memorise

Servants of the People Society → Lala Lajpat Rai

73. National College, Lahore

  • He was associated with the establishment of National College at Lahore.
📌 Must-Memorise

National College Lahore → Lala Lajpat Rai

  • Lajpat Rai led an anti-Simon Commission demonstration at Lahore on 30 October 1928.

Simon Protest Lahore → Lala Lajpat Rai

76. Lathi Charge

  • Police subjected the procession to a severe lathi charge.

77. James A. Scott

  • Revolutionaries blamed Police Superintendent James A. Scott for the lathi charge.

78. Death

  • Lala Lajpat Rai died on 17 November 1928.
📌 Must-Memorise

Lajpat Rai → Died 17 November 1928

79. Saunders Case Link

  • Bhagat Singh and his comrades later planned to kill Scott in retaliation.
  • They mistakenly killed J.P. Saunders.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite

Scott → Intended Target

Saunders → Actual Victim

E. Bipin Chandra Pal

80. Bipin Chandra Pal — Overview

  • Bipin Chandra Pal was an important nationalist journalist, speaker and advocate of Swadeshi.
📌 Must-Memorise

Bipin Chandra Pal → Lal-Bal-Pal + Swadeshi

81. Birth

  • He was born on 7 November 1858 in Sylhet.

82. Lal-Bal-Pal

  • Pal represented the "Pal" in Lal-Bal-Pal.

83. Swadeshi Programme

Pal strongly supported:

  • Boycott.
  • Swadeshi.
  • National education.
  • Passive resistance.

84. Journalism

  • Journalism was a major instrument of Pal's political activity.

85. New India

  • Bipin Chandra Pal was closely associated with the journal New India.
📌 Must-Memorise

New India → Bipin Chandra Pal

86. Bande Mataram

  • He was also associated with nationalist journalism surrounding Bande Mataram.

87. Aurobindo Connection

  • Pal worked in the same assertive Bengal nationalist environment as Sri Aurobindo.

88. Refusal to Testify

  • Pal refused to give evidence against Aurobindo in a colonial prosecution and was imprisoned.

89. Political Thought

  • He argued that freedom required:
  • Self-reliance.
  • National education.
  • Strong public mobilisation.

90. Death

Surendranath Banerjee → Indian Association + The Bengalee

Indian National Conference → Precursor Environment to INC

The Bengalee → Surendranath Banerjee

99. Moderate Politics

A Nation in Making → Surendranath Banerjee

G. Annie Besant

Annie Besant → Home Rule + Theosophical Society + First Woman INC President

103. Theosophical Society

  • Annie Besant joined the Theosophical Society and later became its international president.

Annie Besant → India → 1893

Central Hindu College → Annie Besant

Home Rule League → Annie Besant → 1916

First Woman INC President → Annie Besant → 1917
